title: Crispy mutton (goat) kheema spicy noodles
yield_text: 1 lb goat kheema batch; servings not specified
ingredients: 1 large red onion, finely diced in a food processor
½ small cabbage, finely chopped in a food processor
1 pack wide rice noodles — pack weight not specified
Lao Gan Ma — fermented soybean version preferred
Oil: 1 tsp, then 1–2 tsp, then 1 oil spoonful — spoon size not specified
Water as needed; reserve 1 cup noodle cooking water
steps: Put the kheema in a dry cooking pan. Add salt, a generous amount of black pepper, haldi, hot chili powder, Kashmiri chili powder, Worcestershire sauce, grated ginger and grated garlic. Mix and marinate for 15–20 minutes.
Bring water to a boil and soak the rice noodles.
Brown the kheema over high to medium-high heat until crispy. Transfer to a bowl.
Add 1 tsp oil to the pan, add the onion, salt it and sauté for 30 seconds, scraping up browned bits.
Add the cabbage and continue deglazing. Reduce the heat if the vegetables burn instead of releasing moisture.
Rinse the noodles, reserving 1 cup of noodle cooking water in the pot.
When the onion is translucent and cabbage has softened, push the vegetables to the side. Add 1–2 tsp oil to the center.
When hot, add cumin and toast for 30 seconds without burning. Add grated ginger and garlic and sauté for 5–10 seconds.
Add 1–1½ tbsp kheema masala and 1 oil spoonful of oil. Sauté briefly without burning.
Toss the vegetables with the masala. Add the rice noodles and reserved water. Mix well, add light soy sauce and mix again.
Add the cooked kheema and Lao Gan Ma. Mix, adding water if the noodles need more cooking or liquid is needed for a glaze.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Taste, add coconut aminos and salt, and cook until the water evaporates and the noodles are glazed.
Turn off the heat. Add a splash of rice vinegar and adjust seasonings.
notes: Spices and sauces are to taste where no amount was supplied. Preserve goat kheema and the preferred fermented-soybean Lao Gan Ma. Contains soy; wheat depends on sauce brands.

title: Kerala air-fried chicken

Add the fresh curry leaves and slit chilies during the final 4–5 minutes.
Serve with creamy onions and yogurt dip.

title: Crispy rice tuna salad
ingredients: RICE: 1 tbsp Lao Gan Ma spicy chili crisp
DRESSING: ½ cup Kewpie or regular mayonnaise
SALAD: 2 cans tuna (10 oz drained, as supplied)
½ tbsp sesame seeds, to finish
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Toss the already-cooked rice with the rice oil, chili crisp and soy sauce, and spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 25–45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes; drier rice takes less time.
Mix the dressing ingredients and set aside.
Combine the tuna, cucumber, edamame, avocado, bell pepper and green onions.
Let the crispy rice cool.
Add the rice and dressing to the salad and mix.
Top with sesame seeds and serve.
notes: Tossing the rice with its listed seasonings is made explicit for clarity. Confirm whether “10 oz drained” means the combined tuna weight. Contains fish, soy, sesame and usually egg; wheat depends on brands.
nutrition: User-supplied, not independently verified: 451 kcal; protein 17 g; fat 26 g; carbohydrates 28 g per serving (6 servings).

title: Crispy pork chili oil noodles (Chef Fatty)
yield_text: 1 lb pork and 8 oz dried noodles; servings not specified
ingredients: Garlic powder, for pork — optional annotation; amount not specified
Chinese BBQ seasoning — optional annotation; amount not specified
Crisp-steamed broccoli — optional; quantity not specified
Sliced oyster mushrooms — optional; quantity not specified
SAUCE: 4 garlic cloves, minced (garlic powder was used instead)
steps: Soak the rice noodles in tap-hot water for 10 minutes while preparing the pork and sauce.

If using, mix the pork with Chinese BBQ seasoning and garlic powder. Heat the oil in a large, wide pan over medium-high heat. Spread pork in one layer and leave undisturbed for 2–3 minutes until the bottom caramelizes. Break it apart and cook 3–4 minutes more until crisp at the edges and cooked through. Drain excess fat if needed, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan. Remove the pork.

Add the sauce garlic (or garlic powder), hoisin, soy sauce, chili oil, brown sugar, sesame oil and stock. Add oyster mushrooms if using. Bring to a simmer and reduce for 1–2 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened.
Add the drained noodles and toss for 2–3 minutes until they absorb the sauce and look dark and lacquered. Return the pork, add scallions and toss.
If using broccoli, put the salted, crisp-steamed broccoli in a large bowl. Pour the noodles and sauce over it and mix.
Finish with scallions, sesame seeds and a generous drizzle of chili oil.
notes: Source credit supplied: Chef Fatty. Equipment: large pan. Parenthetical seasonings, garlic-powder substitution and vegetables preserve your annotations. Contains soy and sesame; wheat depends on sauces.

title: Fried fish with curry leaves
yield_text: ½ kg fish batch; servings not specified
ingredients: ½ kg fish, pieces or fillets
FIRST MARINADE: 1 tbsp ginger–garlic paste or grated ginger and garlic
FIRST MARINADE: Lemon juice as needed
FIRST MARINADE: ¼ tsp turmeric powder
FIRST MARINADE: ¾ tsp garam masala or another spice powder
FIRST MARINADE: ½ tsp coriander powder, optional
FIRST MARINADE: ½ tsp red chili powder or smoked paprika
SECOND COATING: 1½ tbsp rice flour or all-purpose flour
SECOND COATING: 1½ tbsp besan (gram flour), or substitute corn flour
SECOND COATING: ¼–½ tsp red chili powder or paprika
SECOND COATING: 1 sprig curry leaves, finely chopped, or other herbs
Sliced onion and grated carrot, to garnish
steps: Mix the first marinade ingredients into a paste. Taste and adjust before the marinade contacts raw fish.
Pat the fish dry; make slits in thick fillets such as salmon if needed. Coat with marinade, adding 1 tsp water if necessary to help it spread. Set aside.
Mix the second-coating ingredients. Coat both sides of the fish in this flour mixture.
Rest for 10–15 minutes until moisture from the fish dampens the flour and helps it adhere.
Heat a griddle, pan or tawa over low heat and spread with 2 tbsp oil. Pan-fry or shallow-fry until crusty on both sides and cooked through, flipping gently to keep the coating intact.
Garnish with sliced onion and grated carrot. Serve with a meal or as an appetizer.
Oven option, as supplied: after coating, brush generously with oil. Preheat the oven at 170°C for 15 minutes, then cook for about 25 minutes, adjusting for fish thickness and type.
notes: Fish and flour choices retained. Preparation is edited to pat fish dry and avoid tasting marinade after contact with raw fish. The supplied oven method calls this “grill”; oven mode was not specified. Contains fish; wheat if all-purpose flour is used.

title: Roasted cauliflower and lentil salad
ingredients: 1 large red or yellow onion, halved and sliced
1 medium cauliflower (about 2 lb), cut into bite-size florets
Handful of fresh cilantro or mint leaves
½ cup sliced or slivered toasted almonds (2 oz)
About 6 cups water, for cooking lentils
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.

Put the onion and cauliflower on a large sheet pan. Toss with 4 tbsp olive oil, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer and roast for 25–30 minutes, tossing halfway, until tender and caramelized.

Meanwhile, put the lentils and garlic in a large pot and cover with about 6 cups water. Salt generously and bring to a boil. Reduce to medium and cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes, until just tender. Drain; toss in the colander or mash the hot garlic with the back of a spoon to break it apart.
In a large serving bowl, stir together the yogurt, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add the cauliflower, lentils, spinach and herbs. Toss and adjust salt and pepper.
Top with toasted almonds. Serve warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
notes: Contains dairy and almonds. Recipe source was not supplied.

title: Taverna salad
ingredients: ⅓ cup plus 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
3 medium tomatoes, cored, seeded and diced into ½-inch pieces, or 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes
1 orange or yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced into ½-inch pieces
½ large English cucumber, seeded and diced into ½-inch pieces
¼ cup minced red onion or shallot
1 block halloumi (8 oz), patted dry and sliced ¾ inch thick
steps: Whisk ⅓ cup olive oil with the vinegar, garlic and oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine the tomatoes, chickpeas, bell pepper, cucumber, olives, parsley, onion, capers and scallions in a large bowl. Toss with the dressing.

Cut the pita into 1-inch pieces. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt. Heat an 8-inch skillet over medium heat and toast the pita for about 5 minutes, tossing often, until golden. Transfer to a bowl and reserve the skillet.

Drizzle the halloumi with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Heat the skillet over medium-high and cook the halloumi for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden. Transfer to a cutting board and cut into bite-size cubes.
Add the pita and halloumi to the salad, toss and serve.
notes: Contains dairy and wheat. Chickpeas and halloumi retained as supplied. Recipe source was not supplied.

title: Pankaj Bhadoria pav bhaji
ingredients: 1 cup finely chopped onions, plus remaining onion for serving
50 g butter, divided, with butter for toasting pav as needed
Turmeric for blanching cauliflower — amount not specified
Water: 1 cup for soaking chilies, ½ cup for garlic water, 1½ cups for bhaji
steps: Deseed the Kashmiri chilies and soak in 1 cup boiling water. Grind into a paste; the grinding step makes the later chili-paste instruction explicit.
Grind the garlic with ½ cup water to make garlic water.

Peel and mash the boiled potatoes. Finely chop the onions, tomatoes, green chilies and capsicum. Mash the boiled beetroot with the vegetables; its use is made explicit because the supplied method does not name it again.
Blanch the cauliflower with salt and turmeric. Blanch the peas, carrots and beans, then drain and coarsely mash the vegetables.
Heat the oil and half the butter. Sauté the onion until light golden. Add pav bhaji masala and capsicum and sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until oil separates.

Add mashed vegetables, potatoes, 2 tbsp red chili paste and 1½ cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 15 minutes, mashing until smooth. Add 2–3 tbsp garlic water and cook 3–4 minutes more.
In a thick-bottomed pan or tawa, heat 1 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp chili paste. Once the chili colors the butter, add 3 ladles bhaji and cook 2–3 minutes.
Split the pavs horizontally and butter the cut sides. Toast on the tawa for about 30 seconds, pressing 2–3 times, until crisp and light brown.
Garnish the bhaji with coriander and remaining butter. Serve with pav, chopped onion and lemon wedges.
notes: Source credit supplied: Pankaj Bhadoria. The listed 20-minute cooking time is retained, although the individual steps may take longer. Total butter allocation and when to add chopped green chilies were not fully specified. Contains dairy and wheat.
